prevention: Parse actor-level and skill expressions as separate grammar tokens.
Accept skill indexes 0 through 17 with min/max ranges.
Do not rewrite a working distribution solely because a static linter disagrees with a clean runtime parse log.
Treat runtime distribution evidence as stronger than a narrower static model.
required_validation: Compare against SPID runtime parse/distribution logs
root_cause: The linter parsed every slash expression as an actor-level range and did not model skillType(min/max) tokens.

sources.note: SPID 7.3.1.16 distributed the For Honor perk using 25/255,0(55/255), while 0(25) produced invalid stoul argument.

symptom: Forge reports Malformed SPID level range for a working filter such as 25/255,0(55/255).
title: Static linter misclassified SPID skill range as actor-level range

regression: tests/test_powershell_release.py plus PowerShell-Parse-Gate.ps1 and the Windows all-provider skill-install job.
root_cause: PowerShell treats the colon as part of a scoped variable reference. Use ${Name}, $($Name), or the format operator.
symptom: ParserError: Variable reference is not valid when a simple variable is immediately followed by a colon inside an expandable string.

prevention: Do not pass standalone -Root "%~dp0" to PowerShell when the script can use $PSScriptRoot.
Reject standalone quoted %~dp0 arguments during repository validation.
Exercise START-HERE.bat --validate-only under Windows CI.
regression: tests/test_powershell_release.py and the Windows exact START-HERE startup-gate job.
root_cause: A quoted %~dp0 token was passed as a standalone argument to an external executable. The expanded value ends with a backslash, which can escape the closing quote in Windows command-line serialization.
symptom: Resolve-Path reports Illegal characters in path and shows a Forge root ending in a literal double quote.

cause: The test recursively scanned every .ps1 below the repository instead of the same Forge-owned source set used by the parser gate.
fix: Audit only top-level Forge scripts and workers/*.ps1; exclude runtime-generated environments.
symptoms: Valid .venv Activate.ps1 reported as ambiguous PowerShell interpolation
Run Tests.bat fails after installation but clean repository tests pass
title: Regression test scans runtime virtualenv PowerShell scripts

cause: Example.psc and example.PSC were created in one case-insensitive directory, so the second write replaced the first.
fix: Place case-equivalent filenames in separate source roots while retaining the same case-insensitive ScriptName identities.
symptoms: PAPYRUS-LOOP-IN-UPDATE warning disappears only on Windows
Duplicate ScriptName test sees only the second file content
title: Case-collision Papyrus fixture overwrites itself on Windows

prevention: Use -buildvcs=false for every release native build
Pin Go 1.23.2
Keep -trimpath and empty buildid
Compare rebuilt hashes to both published and packaged helper copies
required_validation: Build from a temporary Git checkout
root_cause: Go automatically embeds vcs.revision, vcs.time, and vcs.modified when source is inside a Git checkout unless -buildvcs=false is specified.
symptom: Fresh GitHub Actions native builds are deterministic with each other but do not match binaries built from an extracted source tree.
title: Git checkout embeds VCS metadata and breaks native binary reproducibility
